topic_tag: fate of a dissolved guild's hall
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. The hall stood on the only ground in the town above the river's high-water mark. Parish records from the wet springs of 1784, 1802 and 1830 list families from the lower streets who lodged in it for weeks at a time, and between those years the council kept its cellars stocked with grain and blankets. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: Standing above the high-water mark, the hall took in families from the flooded lower streets in wet springs and was kept supplied for that purpose, so it served as the town's "refuge." "Platform" fails because no one addressed the public from the hall; people lived in it. "Ornament" fails because the hall's value lay in sheltering people, not in being admired. "Quarry" fails because the hall was kept whole and stocked, not stripped for its stone.

platform.quote: lodged in it for weeks at a time
platform.why: the hall was used to house people, not as a place from which to speak to the public

ornament.quote: kept its cellars stocked with grain and blankets
ornament.why: the hall was maintained for practical use, not for display

quarry.why: the hall's role depended on the building standing on its high ground, so it was not being broken up for stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. Its long balcony looked down on the square, which farmers from every village in the district crowded into on market days. Before each council election the candidates took turns on that balcony on successive market mornings, and the weekly paper built its election reports from notes its reporters took in the square below. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The balcony overlooked the crowded market square, candidates stood on it in turn before each election, and reporters below took down what they heard, so the hall served as the town's "platform" for addressing the public. "Refuge" fails because no one sheltered in the hall. "Ornament" fails because the hall mattered for what was said from it, not for its looks. "Quarry" fails because the balcony stayed in use election after election, so the building was not being taken apart.

refuge.quote: candidates took turns on that balcony
refuge.why: the hall was used by candidates facing the crowd, not by anyone seeking shelter

ornament.quote: notes its reporters took in the square below
ornament.why: what mattered about the hall was what was heard from it, not its appearance

quarry.why: the balcony was used again at every election, so the building stood intact rather than being stripped for stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. The council repainted its carved front after every hard winter and hung it with lamps on feast days. Its doors stayed locked, and the council minutes record no meeting, sale or service held in or at the hall in those hundred years. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The council kept the hall's front painted and lit while never using the building for anything, so it served the town chiefly as an "ornament," kept up only to be looked at. "Refuge" fails because the doors stayed locked and no one took shelter inside. "Platform" fails because no meeting or gathering was held there. "Quarry" fails because the hall was carefully maintained, not broken up.

refuge.why: no one could shelter in a building that was never opened

platform.quote: no meeting, sale or service held in or at the hall
platform.why: nothing was said to the public from the hall, so it was not a platform

quarry.quote: repainted its carved front after every hard winter
quarry.why: the building was being preserved, not stripped for its stone

worlds.passage: A weavers' guild built a stone hall beside the market square of a river town in 1580, and the guild was dissolved in 1760. No buyer could be found for the building, and within forty years it had lost its roof and most of its upper walls. A survey of the town in 1860 found stones bearing the guild's carved emblem in the foundations of more than sixty houses and in the bridge over the millrace. In the century after 1760, one historian writes, the hall served chiefly as the town's ______.
worlds.explanation: The abandoned hall lost its walls while its carved stones turned up in houses and a bridge across town, so it served as the town's "quarry," a source of building stone. "Refuge" fails because a roofless ruin sheltered no one. "Platform" fails because no one spoke from the hall. "Ornament" fails because the hall was left to fall apart rather than kept up for display; its emblem survived only in pieces built into other structures.

refuge.quote: lost its roof and most of its upper walls
refuge.why: a building without a roof or walls could shelter no one

platform.why: the building stood unused and decaying; nothing suggests anyone addressed the public from it

ornament.quote: in the foundations of more than sixty houses
ornament.why: the carved stones ended up buried in foundations, used as material, not displayed
